prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, which opened moire quantum materials.

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the one candidate that all eight members ranked, four of them in their top three, and I think that breadth reflects real content rather than convenience. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model made a sharp, quantitative prediction in 2011 that the bandwidth collapses at a specific twist angle; the 2018 experiments of Jarillo-Herrero's group then found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. A prediction followed by a clean experimental confirmation is the structure the prize handles best, and the resulting field of tunable moire correlated and topological matter has been independently reproduced in many groups and many materials within a few years. Interaction strength is controlled by a gate and an angle rather than by chemistry, which is a new way to do correlated-electron physics. It is also distinct from the 2025 circuits prize and from the topological-phase prize of 2016. I moved B028 from second to first because my own first choice, B018, has drawn no support in the opening ballots, and because the evidence for B028 is stronger across more independent readers.
statement.case_against: The origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated insulators are still debated, so the most striking phase is not explained. The field is young relative to the other mature candidates, and a prize now might be called early. Attribution is also imperfect: Yuan Cao and the other first authors, and the Dean and Young groups on related moire systems, are not in the credited names, and a three-person limit forces a choice between a theory-experiment pairing and a fuller experimental credit. The strongest alternative is the topological insulator line (B048 or B031), which is more settled but whose credit is tangled by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and by Hasan and Xue.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B028 second, calling the originality and breadth very large but noting that the nature of the correlated states and pairing remains debated and that the credited list omits other contributors such as Dean and coworkers.
responses.response: I agree that the pairing mechanism is open, but I do not think it is the discovery being recognised. The prize would honour the existence of the flat-band regime and the observation that it hosts correlated and superconducting phases, both of which are reproduced and stable. Where I take a different view is on the gap you note: a theory-plus-experiment pair is a coherent unit, and the Dean-group work is better treated as part of the later field than as a missing co-discoverer of the magic-angle effect. I would not wait for the pairing question to be settled, since that could take another decade.

responses.point: Kroll puts optical lattice clocks (B022) first, arguing that the magic-wavelength concept and the 10^-18 performance are clear, original, independently reproduced and timely.
responses.response: I accept that B022 is clean on attribution, and Katori and Ye are an easy two-person allocation, which is a real advantage over my own pick. My reservation is not about quality. It is that the clock case rests on a measurement-precision result whose largest consequences (the redefinition of the second, tests of constants) are still prospective, whereas the moire field has already changed what theorists and experimentalists study in condensed matter. As a condensed-matter theorist I am obviously not a neutral judge of the clock literature, so I would value Lindroth's and Kroll's judgement on whether the fundamental-physics reach is already demonstrated. I keep B022 as a serious option but not as my first choice.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED (B014) first, as foundational to superconducting processors and distinct from the 2025 prize, while acknowledging that it might be judged too close to that prize.
responses.response: I share your worry about proximity, and I would put it more strongly: the 2025 award was about superconducting circuits as macroscopic quantum systems, and giving circuit QED so soon would look like a second prize for one platform. There is also a four-name credit list that does not fit three places cleanly, and Girvin and Blais would be on opposite sides of any cut. I agree that the technology impact is large, but I do not think it outweighs the proximity and attribution problems. I would be glad to be persuaded otherwise if you can show a cleaner three-person allocation than I can.

responses.point: Olsson ranks the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface (B001) first from her direct experience of oxide interfaces and ranks the topological-insulator candidate B031 third, noting that it mixes several sub-results.
responses.response: Your point that B031 mixes the quantum spin Hall effect with the quantum anomalous Hall effect is, I think, the strongest argument against the Kane-Molenkamp-Xue combination: they are two discoveries and the citation would be forced. That is why my own topological alternative is the narrower B048 and not B031. On B001, I take seriously your direct knowledge that oxygen vacancies and cation intermixing complicate the carrier story, since that is exactly the kind of mechanism doubt I am holding against twisted bilayer graphene. I would ask how you weigh that, because the interface discovery is older and still has an unsettled origin, which sits uneasily with maturity as the test.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the Higgs experimental discovery (B037) first as a discovery of the first rank, but accepts that three names cannot fairly represent two collaborations of thousands and that the committee would have to argue the principle.
responses.response: I agree that the physics is of the first rank. My difficulty is the one you raise yourself. Honouring detector conception by three leaders asserts a principle that this committee would have to settle for a collaboration of that size, and the 2012 analysis leaders are a different group from the credited ones. Until the committee settles that principle, I cannot support B037 as a preferred configuration, even though I would not oppose it if the principle were agreed.

uncertainties: Whether a prize now is early given that the origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved.
Whether the experimental credit should include Yuan Cao or others instead of, or alongside, a single senior experimentalist, given the three-name limit.
Whether Bistritzer should be a laureate alongside MacDonald, or whether the strongest configuration is only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero.
Whether the committee is prepared to honour a computational method (B018) as a discovery, and whether the allocation among Metzner, Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar can be settled.
statement.conflict_note: No specific personal or institutional conflict is apparent from my profile for B028, B048 or the other shortlisted candidates. My research field (electronic-structure theory, DFT and correlated electrons) is close to B018, B028 and B048, which is intellectual proximity and not a documented relationship with any credited person.
